note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 43) on data/benches/neutralisation.json: an acid and a base. 1 M sodium hydroxide poured into 25 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid: the solution warms as they neutralise (55.8 kJ a mole of water), the pH hardly moves while acid is left, then leaps from 2 to 12 across the last few mL (40, 8 and 5 mL poured) (chem_tool study neutralisation).
title: Experiment: an acid meets a base

steps.title: A monitor on the acid
steps.text: Drag a monitor out of the parts drawer onto a free square. Drag from its sensing port onto the beaker. Click "vessel", then "pH".
steps.why: The beaker holds 25 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid: 0.05 mol of hydrogen ions. The bottle holds 1 M sodium hydroxide, a base: each NaOH gives a hydroxide ion, OH-.

checks.text: a monitor reads the beaker's pH

steps.title: Above pH 7
steps.text: Click "above". Then click the value, type 7, and click "set".
steps.why: Its lamp lights once the beaker is no longer acid.

steps.title: 40 mL of the base
steps.text: Pick up the base, then right-click the beaker. Drag the menu's slider to about 40 mL, then click "pour".
steps.why: Each hydroxide ion meets a hydrogen ion and they become water: H+ + OH- -> H2O. 40 mL of the base takes 0.04 mol of the 0.05.

steps.title: It warms
steps.text: Point at the beaker: the readout shows its temperature.
steps.why: Making water out of its ions gives out heat, 55.8 kJ for each mole: the neutralisation is exothermic.

steps.title: 8 mL more
steps.text: Pick up the base again, right-click the beaker, slide to about 8 mL and pour.
steps.why: Now 0.048 mol of the 0.05 are gone: only 4 % of the acid is left, yet the pH is still about 2. pH counts in powers of ten.

steps.title: 5 mL more
steps.text: Once more: slide to about 5 mL and pour. Watch the monitor's lamp.
steps.why: 2 mL of these neutralise the last of the acid; the other 3 mL are base left over, and the pH leaps past 7 to about 12. Exactly neutral lies within a drop: that is why a titration ends a drop at a time.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged
